newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end mostly lower with soybeans.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end mostly lower with soybeans.

text.p: CBOT soy product futures finished mostly lower Monday, under pressure from moderate losses in CBOT soybeans, traders said.
The source of weakness in the soy complex was heavy weekend rains in overly dry areas of the central U.S. Midwest, traders said.
Additional pressure stemmed from reports that monsoonal rains in India were preceding normally.
Any adverse affects from the disruptive El Nino weather pattern has not yet been visible this growing season, government officials in India said earlier.
Some weakness in soymeal came from a drop in cash basis offers in spot markets, traders said. Weak demand caused basis in some rail markets to fall as much as $2.00 to $4.00 per ton.
Soyoil was underpinned by talk that this week's cool weather in the Midwest will cut into soyoil yields, traders said.
December soyoil ended down 0.18 cent per lb at 22.45 cents and others were down 0.09 to 0.22. December soymeal was down $0.60 per ton at $198.70 and other months were $1.70 higher to $1.00 lower.
News that U.S. exporters sold 20,000 tonnes of soyoil for shipment to an unknown destination also offer soyoil prices support, traders said.
On the day in soyoil trade, Cargill sold 400 lots December and Goldenberg Hehmeyer sold 100 December and 100 September. Refco bought 100 September and 200 December, pit sources said.
In soymeal trade on the day, Smith Barney bought 400 lots December and 100 lots October and Term Commodities bought 300 lots December. Merrill Lynch sold 300 lots December, pit sources said.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated by CBOT at 19,000 lots, against Friday's 21,625. Soyoil volume was pegged at 13,000 lots, against Friday's 22,431.
